title: Visual commit history
description: Display the commit history as a compact one-line-per-commit list — combine with --graph and --all for a full branch visualisation.

breakdown.meaning: Show commit history
Show each commit on one line (short hash + message)
Draw ASCII graph of branch structure
Show all branches, not just current

flags.description: Compact output: short hash and subject line
Draw text-based graph of commit history
Show all refs (branches, tags)
Limit number of commits shown
Filter by author name or email

output:
* a1b2c3d (HEAD -> main) fix: resolve login bug
* d4e5f6g feat: add user dashboard
| * h7i8j9k (feature/api) feat: REST API endpoints
|/
* k1l2m3n chore: update dependencies
* n4o5p6q initial commit
tip: Alias this: git config --global alias.lg "log --oneline --graph --all --decorate"

title: Interactive rebase
description: Rewrite, squash, reorder, or drop commits in your local history before pushing — the cleanest way to prepare a branch for code review.

breakdown.meaning: Reapply commits on top of another base
Interactive mode — opens editor to modify commits
Go back 3 commits from current HEAD

flags.description: Make a list of commits to be rebased and open in editor
Rebase onto a specific branch/commit
Abort and return to pre-rebase state
Continue after resolving conflicts

output:
pick a1b2c3d feat: add login form
pick d4e5f6g fix: typo in login
pick h7i8j9k feat: add validation

# Commands:
# p, pick = use commit
# s, squash = meld into previous commit
# d, drop = remove commit
tip: Squash fixup commits before merging: change 'pick' to 'squash' or 'fixup'. Never rebase commits already pushed to shared branches.

title: Stash changes temporarily
description: Save uncommitted changes to a stack so you can switch branches without committing.

breakdown.meaning: Stash away changes in working directory
Push a new stash entry (default action)
Add a descriptive message to the stash

flags.description: Save local modifications to a new stash entry
Apply stashed changes and remove from stash list
List all stash entries
Apply stashed changes but keep in stash list
Remove a single stash entry

example: git stash push -m 'WIP: feature work' && git stash list
output:
Saved working directory and index state On main: WIP: feature work
stash@{0}: On main: WIP: feature work
stash@{1}: On main: debugging auth issue
tip: Use 'git stash pop' to apply and remove. Use 'git stash apply stash@{1}' to apply a specific stash without removing it.

title: Cherry-pick a commit
description: Apply the changes from a specific commit onto the current branch — copies the commit without moving the original branch pointer.

breakdown.meaning: Apply changes from an existing commit
The commit hash to cherry-pick

flags.description: Apply changes without creating a commit
Append '(cherry picked from commit ...)' to message
Cancel cherry-pick and restore original state

output:
[main def5678] feat: add error handling
 Date: Tue Mar 12 10:00:00 2024 +0000
 1 file changed, 15 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)
tip: Use -x flag to include the source commit reference in the message. This helps track where cherry-picked commits came from.

command: git bisect start && git bisect bad && git bisect good v1.0
title: Find bug-introducing commit
description: Use binary search to find the exact commit that introduced a bug by marking known good and bad commits.

breakdown.meaning: Begin the bisect session
Run the next command only if the previous one succeeds
Mark the current commit (HEAD) as containing the bug
Mark tag v1.0 as a known good commit without the bug

flags.description: Start a bisect session
Mark a commit as containing the bug
Mark a commit as not containing the bug
End the bisect session and return to the original HEAD
Automatically bisect using a script that returns 0 for good

example: git bisect start && git bisect bad && git bisect good v1.0
output:
Bisecting: 12 revisions left to test after this (roughly 4 steps)
[e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3] feat: refactor auth module

(after testing and marking each commit)

e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3 is the first bad commit
commit e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3
Author: dev@example.com
Date:   Mon Mar 10 14:22:00 2024 +0000

    feat: refactor auth module
tip: Automate bisecting with 'git bisect run ./test.sh' where the script exits 0 for good and non-zero for bad. Always run 'git bisect reset' when done to return to your original branch.

title: Reset HEAD
description: Move the HEAD pointer back one commit while keeping changes staged, allowing you to recommit with a different message or combine commits.

breakdown.meaning: Reset the current HEAD to a specified state
Keep changes staged (in the index) — ready to recommit
One commit before the current HEAD

flags.description: Reset HEAD only; keep index and working tree unchanged
Reset HEAD and index; keep working tree unchanged (default)
Reset HEAD, index, and working tree — discards all changes
Reset index and update working tree files that differ between commit and HEAD

output:
(no output on success — changes are now staged)

$ git status
On branch main
Changes to be committed:
  (use "git restore --staged <file>..." to unstage)
        modified:   src/auth.js
        new file:   src/auth.test.js
tip: Use --soft to undo a commit but keep your changes staged. Use --mixed (default) to unstage as well. Only use --hard when you truly want to discard all changes — it cannot be undone without reflog.

title: Show changes
description: Show the differences between staged changes and the last commit, letting you review exactly what will be committed.

breakdown.meaning: Show changes between commits, working tree, and index
Compare staged changes against the last commit (same as --cached)

flags.description: Show changes staged for the next commit
Show a summary of changes (files changed, insertions, deletions)
Show only names of changed files
Show word-level diff with color highlighting
Ignore all whitespace changes

tip: Use 'git diff' (no flags) to see unstaged changes. Use 'git diff HEAD' to see all changes (staged and unstaged) compared to the last commit.

title: Branch management
description: List all local and remote branches, sorted by most recent commit date to quickly find active branches.

breakdown.meaning: List, create, or delete branches
Show both local and remote-tracking branches
Sort by committer date, newest first (- prefix = descending)

flags.description: List both local and remote-tracking branches
Delete a fully merged branch
Force delete a branch even if not merged
Rename the current branch
Sort branches by a given key (e.g., committerdate, authordate)
Show the last commit hash and message for each branch

output:
* main                           a1b2c3d fix: resolve login bug
  feature/dashboard                d4e5f6g feat: add user dashboard
  bugfix/auth-token                h7i8j9k fix: token expiry handling
  remotes/origin/main              a1b2c3d fix: resolve login bug
  remotes/origin/feature/api       k1l2m3n feat: REST API endpoints
  remotes/origin/release/v2.0      n4o5p6q chore: bump version
tip: Use 'git branch -d feature/done' to delete merged branches. Run 'git remote prune origin' to clean up stale remote-tracking branches that no longer exist on the remote.

title: Manage remotes
description: View, add, rename, and remove remote repository connections — remotes are named references to URLs for pushing and pulling.

breakdown.meaning: Manage set of tracked repositories
Verbose — show remote URLs alongside names

flags.description: Show remote URLs after each name
Add a new remote: git remote add <name> <url>
Remove a remote and its tracking branches
Rename a remote: git remote rename <old> <new>
Change the URL for an existing remote

output:
origin  git@github.com:myorg/myapp.git (fetch)
origin  git@github.com:myorg/myapp.git (push)
upstream  git@github.com:upstream/myapp.git (fetch)
upstream  git@github.com:upstream/myapp.git (push)
tip: Add an upstream remote for forked repos: 'git remote add upstream <original-repo-url>'. Then sync with 'git fetch upstream && git merge upstream/main'.

title: Merge branches
description: Merge a feature branch into the current branch with a merge commit, preserving the branch history in the commit graph.

breakdown.meaning: Join two or more development histories together
Always create a merge commit, even if fast-forward is possible
The branch to merge into the current branch

flags.description: Create a merge commit even when fast-forward is possible
Only merge if fast-forward is possible, otherwise abort
Squash all commits into a single change set without committing
Abort the current merge and restore pre-merge state
Set the commit message for the merge commit

output:
Merge made by the 'ort' strategy.
 src/login.js      | 45 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 src/login.test.js | 32 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 src/auth.js       |  8 ++++++--
 3 files changed, 83 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)
 create mode 100644 src/login.js
 create mode 100644 src/login.test.js
tip: Use --no-ff to preserve feature branch history in the graph. Use --squash for a clean single commit when you don't need individual commit history from the branch.

title: Create tags
description: Create an annotated tag to mark a specific point in history, typically used for release versions.

breakdown.meaning: Create, list, or delete tags
Create an annotated tag (stores tagger info, date, and message)
The tag name — follows semantic versioning
The tag message describing the release

flags.description: Create an annotated tag object
Set the tag message
Delete a tag
List tags matching a pattern: git tag -l 'v1.*'
Show tag message lines when listing

output:
(no output on success)

$ git tag -l -n1
v0.9.0  Beta release
v1.0.0  Release 1.0

$ git show v1.0.0
tag v1.0.0
Tagger: Dev User <dev@example.com>
Date:   Fri Mar 14 10:00:00 2025 +0000

Release 1.0

commit a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0
Author: Dev User <dev@example.com>
Date:   Fri Mar 14 09:55:00 2025 +0000

    feat: finalize v1.0 features
tip: Tags are not pushed by default. Use 'git push origin v1.0.0' to push a specific tag or 'git push origin --tags' to push all tags. Prefer annotated tags (-a) over lightweight tags for releases.

title: Reference log
description: Show the reference log — a history of where HEAD has pointed, including commits, resets, rebases, and other operations. Essential for recovering lost commits.

breakdown.meaning: Manage reference log entries recording when branch tips were updated
Show the log of reference updates (default action)
Show timestamps as relative time (e.g., '2 hours ago')

flags.description: Show the reflog for a given ref (defaults to HEAD)
Format dates: relative, local, iso, short
Limit the number of entries shown
Prune older reflog entries
Delete single reflog entries

output:
a1b2c3d HEAD@{5 minutes ago}: commit: fix: resolve login bug
d4e5f6g HEAD@{2 hours ago}: merge feature/dashboard: Merge made by the 'ort' strategy.
h7i8j9k HEAD@{3 hours ago}: rebase (finish): returning to refs/heads/main
k1l2m3n HEAD@{3 hours ago}: rebase (pick): feat: add validation
n4o5p6q HEAD@{yesterday}: reset: moving to HEAD~2
q7r8s9t HEAD@{yesterday}: commit: feat: add user settings
u1v2w3x HEAD@{2 days ago}: checkout: moving from feature/api to main
tip: The reflog is your safety net. If you accidentally reset or delete a branch, find the lost commit hash in reflog and recover with 'git checkout -b recovered <hash>'. Reflog entries expire after 90 days by default.

title: Clone a repository
description: Create a local copy of a remote repository, including all branches, commits, and tags.

breakdown.meaning: Download a repository from a URL
The remote repository URL

flags.description: Shallow clone — only the latest snapshot
Clone a specific branch
Also clone any submodules

example:
git clone https://github.com/user/repo.git
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/user/repo.git
output:
Cloning into 'repo'...
remote: Counting objects: 1234, done.
Checking out files: 100%, done.
tip: Use '--depth 1' for a shallow clone that skips history — much faster for CI pipelines. Add '--single-branch -b main' to clone only one branch.

title: Initialise a repository
description: Create a new, empty Git repository in the current directory or a specified path, setting up the .git directory.

breakdown.meaning: Create a .git directory and set up a new repo
Set the initial branch name to main

flags.description: Create a bare repository (no working tree)
Set the initial branch name

output: Initialized empty Git repository in /path/to/project/.git/
tip: Use 'git init -b main' to set the default branch name. Run 'git init --bare' to create a remote-style repo without a working tree, suitable for servers.

title: Check working tree status
description: Show the working tree status — which files are staged, unstaged, untracked, or in conflict after a merge.

breakdown.meaning: Show the state of the working directory and staging area

flags.description: Compact output
Show branch info in short format

output:
On branch main
Changes not staged for commit:
  modified:   src/app.ts
Untracked files:
  newfile.txt
tip: Use 'git status -s' for a compact two-column output. Pair with 'git diff --cached' to see exactly what is staged before committing.

title: Stage changes
description: Stage file changes for inclusion in the next commit — supports whole files, directories, or interactive partial staging with -p.

breakdown.meaning: Stage changes for the next commit
Stage all changes in the current directory

flags.description: Stage all changes
Interactively stage chunks of changes
Stage only tracked files (no new files)

example:
git add .
git add src/components/
git add -p
tip: Use 'git add -p' to stage changes in hunks — review each diff fragment individually to build cleaner, atomic commits.

title: Commit staged changes
description: Record staged changes to the repository history with a descriptive message — the basic unit of version control.

breakdown.meaning: Save the staged snapshot to the repo history
Inline commit message

flags.description: Set commit message inline
Modify the most recent commit
Auto-stage tracked modified files before committing

example:
git commit -m "feat: add search bar"
git commit --amend --no-edit
output:
[main 3a2f1b4] feat: add search bar
 2 files changed, 45 insertions(+)
tip: Write commit messages in the imperative mood: 'Add feature' not 'Added feature'. Keep the subject line under 72 chars and add detail in the body.

title: Push commits to remote
description: Upload local commits on a branch to a remote repository, making them available to collaborators.

breakdown.meaning: Upload commits to the remote
The name of the remote (default)
The branch to push

flags.description: Set the upstream for this branch
Safe force push — fails if remote has new commits
Push all tags

example:
git push origin main
git push -u origin feature/my-branch
git push --force-with-lease
output:
To https://github.com/user/repo.git
   3a2f1b4..9c8d2e1  main -> main
tip: Use '--force-with-lease' instead of '--force' when pushing rebased branches — it checks nobody else pushed since you last fetched, preventing accidental overwrites.

title: Pull latest from remote
description: Fetch changes from a remote branch and merge (or rebase) them into the current local branch in one step.

breakdown.meaning: Fetch + merge from remote
Remote name and branch to pull from

flags.description: Rebase instead of merge when pulling
Only fast-forward, never create a merge commit

example:
git pull origin main
git pull --rebase origin main
output:
From https://github.com/user/repo
 * branch  main -> FETCH_HEAD
Updating 3a2f1b4..9c8d2e1
tip: Use 'git pull --rebase' to avoid creating merge commits for routine syncs. Configure as default with 'git config pull.rebase true'.

title: Fetch remote changes
description: Download commits, branches, and tags from a remote without merging anything into the current working branch.

breakdown.meaning: Download objects and refs from remote
Fetch from all remotes
Remove remote-tracking refs that no longer exist

flags.description: Fetch from all configured remotes
Delete stale remote-tracking branches

output:
From https://github.com/user/repo
   3a2f1b4..9c8d2e1  main -> origin/main
tip: Prefer fetch + explicit merge/rebase over git pull for more control. Use 'git fetch --prune' to remove local refs to deleted remote branches.

title: Create and switch branch
description: Switch to an existing branch, updating the working tree to match it — use 'git switch' in Git 2.23+ for a clearer intent.

breakdown.meaning: Switch branches or restore files
Create the branch if it does not exist
Name of the new branch

flags.description: Create and switch to a new branch
Switch to the previously checked-out branch

example:
git checkout -b feature/search
git checkout main
git checkout -
output: Switched to a new branch 'feature/search'
tip: Use 'git checkout -b newbranch' to create and switch in one step. In modern Git, prefer 'git switch branchname' and 'git switch -c newbranch' for clarity.
